newsitem.title: CANADA: Inco Voisey's Bay permit process drags on.
newsitem.headline: Inco Voisey's Bay permit process drags on.

text.p: Inco Ltd said on Thursday the environmental permit process for its Voisey's Bay, Labrador nickel-copper deposit would not likely be concluded before the fourth quarter of 1997.
Inco spokesman David Allen said public hearings into development of the project were under way in Labrador but moving slowly.

"It's dragged extensively. We don't have any firm target for conclusion...they're still, in fact, holding hearings, let alone having to then retire and write the report and then have it translated into six or seven languages, and published and all that. So I mean I think we're really at the end of the fall somewhere," Allen said.

Inco and the governments of Canada and Newfoundland as well as officials representing native groups in Labrador signed a memorandum of understanding for the environmental review of the mining plan at Voisey's Bay in January.
Inco has said construction on the mine and the mill would proceed once the permits were granted.

The Voisey's Bay mine is slated to start producing nickel by 2000. Inco expects production from the mine to be about 270 million pounds by 2001, or about one-third of the company's total production for that year.
